_README: Canonical results registry for the Physis paper portfolio.
Every headline number used in a manuscript MUST appear here as a claim.
Papers cite a claim by ID; no important number lives only as hand-copied prose.
Run `python3 validate.py` to check that (a) every claim traces to a real value
in its result file, and (b) no two papers report incompatible values for the
same claim ID. The validator fails loudly rather than repairing silently.
Status vocabulary: established | suggestive | null | falsified | exploratory | superseded

claims.statement: Corpus size: 75,933 labelled actions across 402 sessions from 4 harnesses on 3 machines, one user.
claims.metric_definition: count of per-action rows carrying an outcome label
claims.null: not applicable - exact count, no test

claims.statement: Session count is 402; median session length is 101 actions; max is 2014.
claims.metric_definition: sessions = distinct session ids; median/max actions per session
claims.note: Previously reported in both papers as median 137; that was wrong. Corrected to 101 on 2026-09-24.
claims.null: not applicable - exact count, no test
claims.threshold: exact session count and per-session size statistics

claims.statement: Cross-harness failure-prior transfer: under session-level bootstrap only 1 of 12 source->target pairs has a CI excluding chance in the positive direction (cline->opencode, 0.534 [0.509,0.559]).
claims.metric_definition: count of pairs whose session-level 95% bootstrap CI lies entirely above AUC 0.5
claims.threshold: session-level 95% bootstrap CI lies entirely above 0.5

claims.statement: Under the action-level bootstrap the same data yields 2 of 12 pairs above chance (cline->opencode and opencode->cline). The action-level bootstrap is the wrong inferential unit for this clustered data.
claims.metric_definition: count of pairs whose action-level 95% bootstrap CI lies entirely above AUC 0.5
claims.uncertainty: action-level bootstrap, 95% CI (reported only to demonstrate the error)
claims.threshold: action-level 95% bootstrap CI lies entirely above 0.5

claims.statement: The action-level bootstrap changes the significance verdict for 4 of the 12 pairs relative to session-level: 3 pairs become distinguishable from chance that were not, and 1 that was distinguishable (significantly below chance) stops being so.
claims.metric_definition: pairs where (session CI contains 0.5) XOR (action CI contains 0.5), split by direction of change
claims.inference_unit: comparison of both units over 12 pairs
claims.uncertainty: exact enumeration over the stored intervals, no resampling
claims.note: THIS IS THE CLAIM THAT WAS PREVIOUSLY INCONSISTENT ACROSS PAPERS. paper9_dataset.tex asserted 'four chance-level comparisons turned apparently significant', which double-counted: only 3 gained significance and 1 lost it, and of the 3 that gained, 2 are significantly BELOW chance, not above. paper1 said 2 (action) vs 1 (session) above chance, which is correct. Fixed 2026-09-24.
claims.null: no change of significance verdict between the two units
claims.threshold: exact enumeration of the 12 stored interval pairs

claims.statement: 6 pairs are significantly below chance under the action-level bootstrap and 5 under session-level; the unlabelled 'does not transfer' headline conceals that most failures are anti-predictive, not merely uninformative.
claims.json_path: DERIVED: count of CIs entirely below 0.5
claims.metric_definition: count of pairs whose 95% CI lies entirely below AUC 0.5

claims.statement: Embedding geometry as a proposer: top-3 containment of the rater's own cell is 0.668 under a random split and 0.541 under a sequential split, against a matched permuted-label null of 0.159 and 0.265 respectively.
claims.metric_definition: fraction of held-out entries whose true cell appears in the top-3 ranked candidate cells
claims.seed: 1000 shuffles for the null; 1000 splits for geometry
claims.threshold: top-k containment exceeds the matched null's top-k

claims.statement: The same representation as a judge: certification AUC on real misfilings is 0.519 (COSINE, n=574), indistinguishable from chance.
claims.metric_definition: ROC AUC distinguishing real misfilings from correct filings
claims.uncertainty: bootstrap CI in the stored file
claims.threshold: certification AUC CI excludes 0.5 (it does not - reported as null)

claims.statement: SUPERSEDED METRIC. A 'propose/certify gap' was previously reported as top-3 containment minus certification AUC (0.668 - 0.519 = +0.149 random; 0.541 - 0.519 = +0.022 sequential). This subtraction is INVALID: containment in {0,1} and ROC AUC are different metrics on different scales, and their difference has no interpretation.
claims.result_file: n/a - this claim is retracted, not measured
claims.note: Removed from paper4 on 2026-09-24. Both tasks are now reported against their OWN matched nulls: the proposer against the permuted-label null, the judge against chance (0.5). The qualitative claim (one task discriminates, the other does not) survives; the numerical gap does not.
claims.null: none - the operation is undefined, this is a retraction

claims.statement: Sequential (file-order) evaluation is the primary protocol; the random split inflates top-3 containment by about +0.13 and is retained only as a labelled optimistic upper bound.
claims.metric_definition: top-3 containment with the first N entries as training and all later entries as test
claims.uncertainty: single deterministic split per fraction; no split-level CI yet
claims.note: refiling_gate0.tsv has a sequence column but no timestamps; this is a SEQUENTIAL split, not a demonstrated chronological one.
claims.null: random train/test split, treated as the optimistic floor

claims.statement: Fine-grained kind labels (871 classes) reach AUC 0.627-0.751 versus coarse tool/prefix labels at 0.446-0.525.
claims.metric_definition: AUC of held-out failure prediction under each label taxonomy
claims.note: Kill test currently reported as point AUCs. Phase 4 of the audit requires session-level CIs around these differences.
claims.null: coarse tool/prefix label taxonomies (133 and 131 classes)
claims.threshold: fine-grained kind AUC exceeds coarse-label AUC

claims.statement: The Empedoclean power-law criticality claim does not survive distribution fitting: a power law never beats a lognormal (Vuong test) at any of 9 settings across 16 seeds, and the critical band at nemesis 0.010 is seed-unstable.
claims.metric_definition: Vuong likelihood-ratio test between power-law and lognormal fits to cluster-size distributions
claims.reproduce: cargo run --release --features empedocles --example empedocles_multiseed && python3 research/papers/fit_empedocles.py
claims.null: lognormal, against the claim's own power law
claims.threshold: power law beats lognormal on Vuong (it never does)

claims.statement: No cross-harness pair shows positive transfer after family-wise (Holm) correction over the 12 comparisons. The three pairs surviving Holm are significantly BELOW chance (claude-code->codex 0.394, codex->cline 0.401, codex->opencode 0.416). cline->opencode (0.534, raw p=0.0094) fails Holm, whose threshold at its rank is 0.006; it survives Benjamini-Hochberg only.
claims.metric_definition: Holm step-down over session-level bootstrap p-values, alpha=0.05, family of 12 directional tests
claims.note: This overturns the earlier headline that 1 of 12 pairs was established. That claim (XFER-001) counted raw CI exclusion without multiplicity control and is now reporting-only.
claims.null: chance, AUC = 0.5, family of 12 directional tests

claims.statement: WITHDRAWN: the cold-start crossover curve previously reported (transferred-only 0.469 -> own-only 0.720, crossover at n=2) is contaminated by train/test leakage. own_only built its prior from all 42 target sessions and was scored on those same 42; mixed_nN scored on tgt including the tgt[:n] used to build it. Only the transferred-only arm (n=0, prior from a different harness) is uncontaminated, and it sits below chance at 0.469 [0.445,0.490].
claims.metric_definition: AUC of failure prediction on claude-code using a prior built from tgt[:n] -- local arms leak
claims.uncertainty: session bootstrap CI; interval valid, point estimate contaminated for the local arms
claims.note: The corrected paired experiment (held-out train/test, arms A/B/C/D) is specified in research/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md item 2 and is NOT yet run.
claims.null: none - claim withdrawn for train/test leakage
claims.threshold: not applicable, retained as an error record

claims.statement: Corrected, leak-free cold-start experiment: with priors built only on a held-out 30-session training pool and all arms scored on a fixed 12-session held-out test set (6,132 actions), the borrowed prior sits below chance at every history size (0.483) and never contributes, while local-only reaches 0.600 at N=2 and 0.656 at N=20, beating the borrowed prior by +0.114 [+0.040,+0.153] at N=2. 15 of 18 paired differences exclude zero. There is NO regime in which borrowing helps.
claims.metric_definition: AUC of per-kind failure prediction on a fixed held-out test set; paired session-level bootstrap CI on the difference from the borrowed-only arm
claims.uncertainty: paired session-level bootstrap, 2000 resamples, on the difference
claims.note: Supersedes the withdrawn curve in XFER-006. Arm A (local-only) is undefined at N=0 and is recorded as null rather than substituted, so its diff is not computed there.
claims.null: the borrowed-only arm (opencode prior, no target data)
claims.threshold: paired session-level bootstrap CI on local-minus-borrowed excludes 0
